target_customer: Smallholder farmers in Nigeria (and expanding in Africa) needing finance, inputs and market access; buyers of grain; commercial lenders
problem: Smallholder farmers lack capital, quality inputs and premium markets, causing low yields and income.
business_model: Farm financing and input supply plus commodity marketplace and aggregation (supply chain take)

founders.name: Uka Eje
founders.background_notes: Grew up in a farming community in Benue.

technical_complexity.rationale: Platform and field-agent operations were mostly logistics and credit operations, not deep technology.

defensibility.rationale: Field-agent network, warehouses (450+ reported by 2023) and farmer data build operational advantage, but the crowdfunding model was copied widely.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Peers in agric crowdfunding largely folded or faced fraud claims after 2020 per TechCabal (2022); Thrive exited crowdfunding.

market_need_then: Over 32 million small farmers in Nigeria, many underserved by finance; Thrive reported funding farmers with over N180M by February 2019 and 50% month-on-month growth (Condia, March 2019).

identity.voice_and_tone: Impact-oriented; tagline about farmers accessing finance, insight and markets.

branding.community_and_virality: A Medium post announced YC acceptance in 2019; a 2020 report mentions about 36 investors issuing an ultimatum over unpaid N50M, which hurt reputation.

brand_strength.rationale: Well covered in African tech and agri press and YC-backed, but investor-repayment disputes in 2020 are reported.

pivots.to: Agricultural operating system, marketplace and supply chain
pivots.why: TechCabal (Feb 2022) says Thrive exited crowdfunding after the sector's fraud and repayment problems; exact date unsourced

outcome_analysis: Thrive Agric started as a farm-crowdfunding platform, joined YC in W19, survived the 2020 collapse of agric crowdfunding by moving into a financing, input supply and grain marketplace model, and raised $56.4M in debt in March 2022 plus commercial paper in August 2026. It reports $100M in loans to 514,000 farmers. Risks include debt-heavy funding and earlier investor disputes.
notes: YC W19 standard deal ($150K for 7%, per Condia March 2019) is not recorded as a round. A snippet says a $9M raise in 2020 preceded the 2022 debt; unverified. Aggregators list conflicting totals ($56.4M, $59M, $67.5M) and a 500 Startups seed; unverified. Pre-seed date given only as 2017 by AgFunder. Commercial paper amount is N5.3bn (about $3.93M per outlet conversion) from search snippets of WeeTracker and Innovation Village. Farmcrowdy competitor source is a 2019 blog; exact seed date from Moguldom not fetched. Name origin not found.
